releases.body:
### Added

- Release candidates. A tag `vX.Y.Z-rc` builds and publishes like a release,
  marked as a pre-release, with its container image tagged `latest-rc`; the
  `latest` aliases do not move. `shoulderd update --rc` takes the newest
  candidate; without the flag a candidate is never offered, and a candidate
  build is told of the release that follows it.
### Changed

- The prompt hook asks the model about the prompt before the assistant reads
  it. One call, no tools, the prompt and the stored rules alone, three
  seconds for the first ask and a retry together; on a timeout or a refusal
  the hook answers as before and the background consult still runs. Context
  the background consult wrote for "the next prompt" used to land on a
  prompt minutes later, about something else. The hook script gives the
  prompt post four seconds instead of two; every other post keeps two.
- A text that reached the assistant is not said again for ten main-thread
  events, five prompts with their answers. The decision model read a stored
  rule on every event it bore on and said it every time.
- Context written for the next prompt is for that prompt alone: when the
  prompt arrives, the one note it takes is delivered and the rest are
  dropped, and a note older than two minutes is dropped unread.
- A decision answer that is not the decision object is asked for once more
  before it counts as a failure. The second ask shows the model the start of
  what it wrote and tells it to answer with the JSON object only. The small
  Gemini model answers the transcript in the editor's voice now and then,
  and one such answer flipped the daemon to "model down" until the next
  event. A refused retry is still one failure, logged and noticed once. The
  retry is counted in `shoulder_advisor_retry_total`.

### Changed

- Every request to the model asks for JSON at the wire: the chat completion
  payload carries `response_format: {"type":"json_object"}` for the
  decision, the tidying pass, `learn`, `message`, `digest` and the start-up
  probe. A model that answered with a stored fact or a tool result instead
  of the decision object did so after a tool call; told at the API level
  that only JSON is accepted, it is far less likely to.
- `message` and `digest` answer inside JSON, `{"answer":""}` and
  `{"digest":""}`, and the daemon reads the field. A prose answer is refused
  with `no JSON object in model output`, counted on the existing error
  metric and logged with the first 400 characters of what the model wrote.
- A decision object with none of the expected keys, `inject`, `facts` or
  `keywords`, and a `message` or `digest` object without its field, are
  refused with an error instead of being read as an empty answer.

### Changed

- The licence is the GNU General Public License, version 3, where it was
  MIT: the repository, the Claude Code plugin, the OpenCode plugin and the
  container image say so.

### Fixed

- A decision the daemon could not read as JSON was logged with the error
  alone, and what the model had written instead was thrown away. The
  `decision failed` log line now carries the first 400 characters of it,
  on one line, as `output`. The notice in the editor is unchanged: the
  text is for the log, not the harness.

### Added

- `shoulderd update` brings the binary to the newest release. A plugin or
  release install has its binary replaced after a check against the
  published `SHA256SUMS`, a `go install` build is installed again, and a
  checkout or a container is told what to run. `--check` only asks and
  exits 3 when a newer release is out.
- The Claude Code plugin's `SessionStart` hook says, once a day, when a
  newer release is out. It does not install it: the place where the harness
  would is a stub in `scripts/ensure-daemon.sh`, empty on purpose.
- The install guide has an update section: the binary, the adapter and the
  process, and what moves each.
- Notices in the editor, on by default. The daemon tells the person what
  it does, as it does it: errors, advice injected with its text, facts
  stored with their text, and facts superseded. `warnings` (a fact that
  could not be kept, and why) and `maintenance` (tidying passes, with
  counts) are named to switch on with `SHOULDER_NOTIFY`; `all` is
  everything, `off` is silence. Claude Code shows them as `systemMessage`, the one hook field
  addressed to the person and never the model; OpenCode shows them as
  toasts. A notice is queued for the session it concerns and rides on that
  session's next hook. `shoulderd doctor` prints the setting in use.

### Fixed

- `shoulderd doctor` told a plugin install that the plugin fetches a newer
  release on the next editor start. It never did: the start script fetches
  only when there is no binary at all. The hint now says `shoulderd update`.

### Added

- The daemon keeps the last word its decision model gave. It asks the model
  one question when it starts and after every `config set` that changes the
  model, and records every decision call after that. A model that refuses -
  a dead key, say - used to leave a daemon that looked healthy from every
  angle while nothing was learned from any session; one ran that way for
  thirteen days.
- `shoulderd doctor` reports a refusing model with the cause, since when and
  how many calls in a row, and exits 1. A model that answers is reported with
  since when. The report used to say only which model was configured.
- `/readyz` carries `model`, `model_provider` and `model_since`. The status
  code is unchanged: no restart mends a dead key.
- `shoulderd monitor` shows every decision the model refused and every
  tidying pass that failed, as `failed`, with the refusal on one line, and
  the model going down and coming back as `model down` and `model up`. The
  view filtered these out before, which is how thirteen days of refusals
  went unseen.
- The Claude Code plugin's `SessionStart` hook tells you when the decision
  model refuses, as the `systemMessage` of the one JSON object it prints.
  Everything the start script said on stderr before went nowhere: the
  harness shows a person nothing from a hook that exits 0 except that
  field, so every warning the script has is now said that way at session
  start.
- `docs/AGENT-SETUP.md` is the install and setup procedure written for the
  coding agent to follow, in Claude Code or OpenCode: hooks, daemon, model,
  key, start, and a doctor report. The README's install section opens with
  the one line to paste into either agent.

### Changed

- `shoulderd monitor` prints the date with the time. A log spans days, and a
  clock time alone could not say which day a movement belonged to.
